cohort: Pregnant women with preterm labor were included and categorized based on their mode of delivery.
finding: The study found that vaginal delivery in preterm births was associated with more favorable early neonatal outcomes, including lower incidences of RDS, neonatal jaundice, ventilator dependence, and PDA in AGA infants, compared to cesarean section.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery in preterm births was associated with more favourable early neonatal outcomes compared to cesarean section, particularly regarding respiratory function, hemodynamic stability, and metabolic adaptation.
birth_weight: Appropriate for gestational age (AGA) and Large for gestational age (LGA) infants
gest_age: Preterm births, stratified by gestational age (<=24, 25-27, 28-30, 31-33, and 34-36 weeks)
